claims.text: H&P (admission) — Admission H&P timing: completed and documented no more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission, and before surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia; it must be in the chart within 24 hours after admission.
claims.quote: (A) A medical history and physical examination completed and documented no more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission or registration, but prior to surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia services, and except as provided under paragraph (c)(4)(i)(C) of this section. The medical history and physical examination must be placed in the patient's medical record within 24 hours after admission or registration, but prior to surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia services.

claims.text: H&P (admission) — Updated exam: if the H&P was done within the 30 days before admission, document an updated exam noting any changes in the patient's condition within 24 hours after admission (and before surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia).
claims.quote: (B) An updated examination of the patient, including any changes in the patient's condition, when the medical history and physical examination are completed within 30 days before admission or registration, and except as provided under paragraph (c)(4)(i)(C) of this section. Documentation of the updated examination must be placed in the patient's medical record within 24 hours after admission or registration, but prior to surgery or a procedure requiring anesthesia services.

claims.text: H&P (admission) — Admitting diagnosis: the record must document it.
H&P (admission) — Every entry: legible, complete, dated, timed and authenticated (written or electronic) by the person responsible for the service.
claims.quote: (1) All patient medical record entries must be legible, complete, dated, timed, and authenticated in written or electronic form by the person responsible for providing or evaluating the service provided, consistent with hospital policies and procedures.

claims.text: Progress note — What the record must show: information that justifies admission and continued hospitalization, supports the diagnosis, and describes the patient's progress and response to medications and services.
claims.quote: The medical record must contain information to justify admission and continued hospitalization, support the diagnosis, and describe the patient's progress and response to medications and services.

claims.text: Progress note — Problem status today: for inpatient and observation care, the problem addressed is its status on the date of the encounter, which may differ greatly from admission, and it may not be the cause of admission or continued stay.
claims.quote: For hospital inpatient and observation care services, the problem addressed is the problem status on the date of the encounter, which may be significantly different than on admission. It is the problem being managed or co-managed by the reporting physician or other qualified health care professional and may not be the cause of admission or continued stay.
claims.locator: Number and Complexity of Problems Addressed, definitions

claims.text: Progress note — Progress: document the patient's progress, response to and changes in treatment, and any revision of the diagnosis.
claims.quote: You should document the patient's progress, response to and changes in treatment, and revision of diagnosis

claims.text: Progress note — Complications: document complications, hospital-acquired infections, and unfavorable reactions to drugs and anesthesia.
claims.quote: (iv) Documentation of complications, hospital acquired infections, and unfavorable reactions to drugs and anesthesia.

claims.text: Consult — Consult results: the hospital record must contain the results of all consultative evaluations of the patient.
claims.quote: (iii) Results of all consultative evaluations of the patient and appropriate findings by clinical and other staff involved in the care of the patient.

claims.text: Consult — Billing a consult (Medicare): Medicare doesn't pay the CPT consultation codes (inpatient 99252-99255, office/outpatient 99242-99245); report the correct E/M visit code for the consult instead.
claims.quote: Medicare doesn't recognize these CPT codes for Part B payment purposes: Inpatient consultation codes, CPT codes 99252-99255 O/O consultation codes, CPT codes 99242-99245 Medicare recognizes these telehealth consultation codes for payment: HCPCS codes G0406-G0408 HCPCS codes G0425-G0427 If you provide services using CPT consultation codes, you should report the correct E/M visit code to bill for these services.

claims.text: D/C (discharge summary) — Discharge summary: outcome of the hospitalization, disposition of the case, and provisions for follow-up care; the final diagnosis is recorded and the record completed within 30 days after discharge.
claims.quote: (vii) Discharge summary with outcome of hospitalization, disposition of case, and provisions for follow-up care. (viii) Final diagnosis with completion of medical records within 30 days following discharge.

claims.text: D/C (discharge summary) — Discharge planning evaluation: goes in the medical record, and its results are discussed with the patient or their representative.
claims.quote: (3) The discharge planning evaluation must be included in the patient's medical record for use in establishing an appropriate discharge plan and the results of the evaluation must be discussed with the patient (or the patient's representative).

claims.text: D/C (discharge summary) — Hand-off at discharge: send the necessary medical information on the current course of illness and treatment, post-discharge goals of care and treatment preferences to the post-acute providers and practitioners responsible for follow-up care.
claims.quote: The hospital must discharge the patient, and also transfer or refer the patient where applicable, along with all necessary medical information pertaining to the patient's current course of illness and treatment, post-discharge goals of care, and treatment preferences, at the time of discharge, to the appropriate post-acute care service providers and suppliers, facilities, agencies, and other outpatient service providers and practitioners responsible for the patient's follow-up or ancillary care.
